summary: Hermann Wilhelm Ebel was a linguist who studied at Halle-Wittenberg and Berlin under Franz Bopp, August Boeckh, and August Friedrich Pott. He taught at Beheim-Schwarzbach'sche Realschule and Gymnasium Schneidemühl before succeeding Bopp in Berlin's chair of comparative philology in 1872.

Heymann Steinthal was a scholar of linguistics and philosophy who studied under August Boeckh at the University of Berlin (~1843–1847). He later held posts at the University of Berlin (~1850–1899) and the Hochschule für die Wissenschaft des Judentums (~1872–1899).
Hideaki Kimura is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he was also attested as a researcher in 1995.

Hideaki Nakatani is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics scholar. He studied under Yutaka Ochihara and Gadjin M. Nagao at Kyoto University and earned a PhD from Sorbonne Nouvelle University. He held a professorship at Kobe Gakuin University (attested 2003).
Hidehiko Kurita works in religious studies and Japanology. He earned a PhD from Tohoku University and was attested as a lecturer at Aichi Prefectural University in 2020.
Hideki Kiyoshima is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at the University of Delhi. He was attested as a lecturer at Kindai University in 1989.

Hideki Yukawa studied at Kyoto University (~1926–1929) and Osaka University (~1934–1938). He held academic posts at Kyoto University (~1932–1970), Osaka University (~1933–1939), the University of Tokyo (~1939–1950), and Columbia University (~1949–1953).
Hidemasa Nagata was a historian and Sinologist who studied at Kyoto University from ~1952 to 1961 and later held a post there from ~1976 to 1996.

Hidenaka Tanaka was a linguist who studied under Raphael von Koeber at the University of Tokyo, at Kyoto University, and at Oxford. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Kyoto University, and Kyoto Women's University.
Hidenori Kitagawa was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He was a Rockefeller Foundation fellow (1952–1953) and served as a professor at Nagoya University (attested 1968–1969).

Hidenori Sakuma, a Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology scholar, studied at the University of Tokyo and earned a PhD under Lambert Schmithausen at Hamburg. He held posts at International Buddhist University, Otani, Taisho, and the University of Tsukuba.

Hideo Mineshima was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Taisho and Waseda Universities. He held professorships at Waseda University (1968–1998) and Bunkyo Gakuin University (~1964–1998), as well as leadership posts in several academic and religious societies.
Hideo Sakurai was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1940–1943) and served as a professor emeritus at Komazawa University (~1950–1987).

Hideomi Yaita is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University. He held positions as a research assistant at Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 1991–1995) and lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1995).
Hidetaka Fukazawa is a religious studies scholar who studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1975–1979) and held a post at Hitotsubashi University (~1990–2021).
Hidetaka Nakatani is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Kyoto University in 1966 under Gadjin M. Nagao.
Hideto Ono is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Komazawa University (~1963–1973) and served as an assistant professor at Aichi Gakuin University (~1985–1993).

Hidetomo Yoshizawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who held several posts at Taisho University, including researcher (attested 1998), research student (attested 2006), lecturer (attested 2008), and chief research fellow (attested 2017).

Hidetsugu Yagi studied at the University of Tokyo (~1906–1909) and later held posts at Tohoku University (~1919–1933), Osaka University (~1933–1946), Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1942–1944), and the University of Tokyo (~1944–1945).

Hideyo Ogawa is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Hiroshima University (~1973–1982). He served there as an assistant professor (~1989–2004) and later as professor in the Graduate School of Letters (~2004–2020).
